**Package:** `SingleCellTools`
**Data:** Illustrative — CellRanger-ATAC output directories (`peaks.bed`, `singlecell.csv`,
`fragments.tsv.gz` under an `outs/` subfolder), the same generic-path convention the main
scRNA-seq vignette uses rather than one specific downloadable dataset. `CreateATACObjects()`
takes raw fragment files as input, which isn't something a one-line `SeuratData::LoadData()`
call can provide the way it does for the `ifnb`/`stxBrain` vignettes -- so this walkthrough is
written against a generic 4-sample, 2-condition design (`Vehicle` x2, `DrugA` x2), matching the
main vignette's own treatment/condition setup, and every call uses this package's real function
signatures.
**Goal:** Walk through a complete scATAC-seq workflow — object creation, QC, dimensionality
reduction, cross-sample integration, gene activity scoring, motif enrichment, and differential
accessibility.

> **Mouse (`mm10`) or human (`hg38`).** `CreateATACObjects()`/`CreateATACObjectsFilter()` take a
> `genome = c("mm10", "hg38")` argument that selects the matching gene annotation
> (`EnsDb.Mmusculus.v79`/`EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86`) and genome sequence
> (`BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10`/`BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38`) package -- `"mm10"` is the
> default. Both genomes' packages are optional (Suggests): only the one matching whichever
> `genome` you actually request needs to be installed, and you'll get an actionable
> `BiocManager::install(...)` error naming it if it's missing. For any other organism/build, build
> the `ChromatinAssay` yourself following Signac's own vignette instead of these two functions;
> everything from Section 4 onward here applies to any genome once you have a Seurat object
> carrying an ATAC peak assay, regardless of how it was built.

## 1. Setup

### Install required packages

```r
# SingleCellTools
remotes::install_github("gevensen95/SingleCellTools")

# Bioconductor dependencies CreateATACObjects()/CreateATACObjectsFilter() use internally.
# GenomicRanges/IRanges/GenomeInfoDb/Signac are required regardless of genome; only
# install the EnsDb/BSgenome pair matching whichever `genome` you'll actually use.
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("Signac", "GenomicRanges", "IRanges", "GenomeInfoDb"))
BiocManager::install(c("EnsDb.Mmusculus.v79", "BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10"))  # genome = "mm10"
# BiocManager::install(c("EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86", "BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38"))  # genome = "hg38"

# Cross-sample integration (Section 5)
install.packages("harmony")

# Motif enrichment (Section 8) -- not required for Sections 1-7
BiocManager::install(c("JASPAR2020", "TFBSTools", "chromVAR", "motifmatchr"))
```

### Load libraries

```r
library(SingleCellTools)
library(Signac)
library(Seurat)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
```

---

## 2. Loading — `CreateATACObjects()`

`CreateATACObjects()` expects each element of `data_dirs` to be a standard
`cellranger-atac count` output folder -- i.e. it looks for `<dir>/outs/peaks.bed`,
`<dir>/outs/singlecell.csv`, and `<dir>/outs/fragments.tsv.gz` (with its `.tbi` index
alongside it, required by Signac's fragment-reading functions even though it isn't
passed explicitly). Point `data_dirs` straight at CellRanger's own output -- no
renaming or reorganizing needed.

```r
data_dirs <- c("data/atac/sample1", "data/atac/sample2",
              "data/atac/sample3", "data/atac/sample4")

atac_list <- CreateATACObjects(
  data_dirs            = data_dirs,
  add_treatment        = TRUE,
  treatment            = c("Vehicle", "Vehicle", "DrugA", "DrugA"),
  genome               = "mm10",   # default -- pass "hg38" for human data
  passed_filters_value = 500
)
names(atac_list)   # basename(data_dirs) -- "sample1", "sample2", "sample3", "sample4"

# Or, for human data, with custom list names instead of basename(data_dirs):
atac_list_human <- CreateATACObjects(
  data_dirs    = c("data/atac/donor1", "data/atac/donor2"),
  genome       = "hg38",
  object_names = c("Donor1", "Donor2")
)
```

Behind the scenes, this:

1. Reads each sample's `peaks.bed` and builds one **combined peak set** across all
   `data_dirs` (`GenomicRanges::reduce()` on the union, kept within
   `[peakwidths_min, peakwidths_max]`, default `[20, 10000]`), so every sample's counts
   land on the same peak coordinates from the start -- no separate peak-reconciliation
   step needed later.
2. Drops peaks on scaffolds/contigs not in the standard mouse chromosomes.
3. Loads gene annotations from `EnsDb.Mmusculus.v79` and attaches them via
   `Signac::Annotation()`.
4. Builds a per-sample `ChromatinAssay` + `Seurat` object (assay name `"ATAC"`) from
   that sample's own fragments against the shared peak set, keeping only cells with
   `passed_filters > passed_filters_value` from `singlecell.csv`.
5. Computes `nucleosome_signal`, `TSS.enrichment`, `pct_reads_in_peaks`, and
   `blacklist_ratio` per cell.
6. Prints an unfiltered 5-panel QC boxplot (one panel per metric, grouped by sample)
   so you can eyeball where reasonable cutoffs might fall before filtering anything.

```r
# Per-sample cell/peak counts
sapply(atac_list, dim)

# QC metrics live in metadata, same shape as any Seurat object
head(atac_list$sample1@meta.data[, c("passed_filters", "peak_region_fragments",
                                     "pct_reads_in_peaks", "TSS.enrichment",
                                     "nucleosome_signal", "blacklist_ratio")])
```

> **On `ConvertToBPCells()`/`on_disk` and ATAC data.** Unlike
> `CreateRNAObjects()`/`CreateVisiumObjects()`/`LoadXenium2()`,
> `CreateATACObjects()`/`CreateATACObjectsFilter()` don't have an `on_disk`
> argument, and calling `ConvertToBPCells()` on the `"ATAC"` assay here errors
> deliberately rather than attempting it. The `"ATAC"` assay is a Signac
> `ChromatinAssay`, not a standard Seurat assay -- it carries
> fragments/ranges/annotation slots that `ConvertToBPCells()`'s generic
> `Assay5` coercion has no way to preserve, so this is a real, checked
> limitation rather than an oversight. See
> [`SingleCellTools_vignette_bpcells.md`](SingleCellTools_vignette_bpcells.md)
> for what is and isn't covered.

---

## 3. QC and Filtering

### 3.1 `CreateATACObjectsFilter()`

`CreateATACObjectsFilter()` does everything `CreateATACObjects()` does, plus an
explicit filtering step -- either fixed cutoffs in one call, or an interactive
prompt-per-metric session. It rebuilds the combined peak set and every object from
the raw CellRanger output again (it doesn't take `atac_list` as input), so treat it
as an alternative entry point from Section 2, not a follow-up step on `atac_list`.

```r
# Fixed cutoffs in one call
atac_list_filtered <- CreateATACObjectsFilter(
  data_dirs                 = data_dirs,
  treatment                 = c("Vehicle", "Vehicle", "DrugA", "DrugA"),
  filter                    = TRUE,
  interactive               = FALSE,
  genome                    = "mm10",   # default -- pass "hg38" for human data
  peak_region_fragments_min = 3000,
  peak_region_fragments_max = 100000,
  pct_reads_in_peaks_min    = 40,
  blacklist_ratio_max       = 0.025,
  nucleosome_signal_max     = 4,
  TSS.enrichment_min        = 2
)

# Or: interactive mode -- prompts once per metric, offering either a quantile
# or an absolute threshold, and re-subsets before asking the next question
atac_list_filtered <- CreateATACObjectsFilter(data_dirs = data_dirs, interactive = TRUE)
```

If you already built `atac_list` in Section 2 and just want to apply fixed thresholds
without re-reading fragments from disk (`CreateATACObjectsFilter()`'s peak-building
and fragment-reading steps are the slow part), subset it directly instead:

```r
atac_list_filtered <- lapply(atac_list, function(obj) {
  subset(obj, subset =
           peak_region_fragments > 3000 & peak_region_fragments < 100000 &
           pct_reads_in_peaks > 40 & blacklist_ratio < 0.025 &
           nucleosome_signal < 4 & TSS.enrichment > 2)
})
```

### 3.2 Alternative: `GenerateQCReport()` / `ApplyQCFilters()`

`GenerateQCReport()`/`ApplyQCFilters()` (used for RNA/spatial QC elsewhere in this
package) are modality-agnostic -- they work directly off whatever metadata columns
you point them at, so they apply to ATAC's `TSS.enrichment`/`nucleosome_signal`/
`pct_reads_in_peaks` exactly the way they apply to RNA's `nFeature_RNA`/`percent.mt`.
This path gives you MAD-based suggested cutoffs per sample (rather than picking fixed
numbers yourself) and a saved cutoffs CSV you can review or edit before applying:

```r
GenerateQCReport(
  atac_list,
  metadata_cols = c("passed_filters", "peak_region_fragments", "pct_reads_in_peaks",
                    "TSS.enrichment", "nucleosome_signal", "blacklist_ratio"),
  output_file   = "atac_qc_report.html",
  title         = "scATAC-seq QC report"
)

# Review/edit atac_qc_report_cutoffs.csv if needed, then apply
atac_list_filtered <- ApplyQCFilters(atac_list, cutoffs = "atac_qc_report_cutoffs.csv")
```

---

## 4. Per-Sample Normalization and Dimensionality Reduction (LSI)

ATAC data is normalized and reduced differently from RNA: term frequency-inverse
document frequency (TF-IDF) instead of log-normalization, and latent semantic
indexing (LSI, an SVD on the TF-IDF matrix) instead of PCA. `SingleCellTools` doesn't
wrap this step -- it's plain Signac, run once per sample before merging so each
sample's own top features are used going in:

```r
atac_list_filtered <- lapply(atac_list_filtered, function(obj) {
  obj <- RunTFIDF(obj)
  obj <- FindTopFeatures(obj, min.cutoff = "q0")   # keep all peaks; raise for a stricter set
  obj <- RunSVD(obj)
  obj
})
```

Check whether the first LSI component just tracks sequencing depth (common, and worth
knowing about before using it for clustering/UMAP):

```r
DepthCor(atac_list_filtered$sample1)
```

If component 1 correlates strongly with depth (`|correlation| > ~0.5` is the usual
rule of thumb), drop it from downstream `dims` -- e.g. use `2:30` instead of `1:30`,
as this vignette does from here on.

---

## 5. Merging and Cross-Sample Integration

`MergeSeurat()` does **not** support ATAC objects -- its normalization
(`SCTransform`/`NormalizeData`) and reduction (`RunPCA`) steps are RNA-specific, and
its `spatial` argument only recognizes `'no'`/`'Visium'`/`'Xenium'`. Merge and
integrate ATAC samples directly with Signac + `harmony`, following the same
LSI-then-batch-correct pattern Signac's own multi-sample vignette uses. Because
`CreateATACObjects()` already put every sample on the same combined peak set, a plain
`merge()` is enough to combine them -- no separate peak-reconciliation step needed:

```r
combined <- merge(atac_list_filtered[[1]], atac_list_filtered[-1],
                  add.cell.ids = names(atac_list_filtered))

combined <- RunTFIDF(combined)
combined <- FindTopFeatures(combined, min.cutoff = "q0")
combined <- RunSVD(combined)
DepthCor(combined)   # re-check on the merged object
```

Batch-correct across samples on the LSI embedding with `harmony::RunHarmony()` --
the same direct-`RunHarmony()` approach `MergeSeurat()` uses for RNA/spatial data,
since current CRAN `harmony` no longer exports the legacy `HarmonyMatrix()` that
`Seurat::IntegrateLayers(method = "HarmonyIntegration")` depends on:

```r
combined <- harmony::RunHarmony(
  combined,
  group.by.vars  = "orig.ident",
  reduction.use  = "lsi",
  dims.use       = 2:30,           # drop LSI-1 if DepthCor() showed strong depth correlation
  reduction.save = "harmony"
)
```

---

## 6. Clustering and UMAP

```r
combined <- RunUMAP(combined, reduction = "harmony", dims = 2:30)
combined <- FindNeighbors(combined, reduction = "harmony", dims = 2:30)
combined <- FindClusters(combined, algorithm = 3, resolution = 0.5)   # SLM -- Signac's recommended algorithm for LSI-based clustering

DimPlot(combined, label = TRUE) + ggtitle("ATAC clusters")
DimPlot(combined, group.by = "orig.ident") + ggtitle("By sample -- should be interleaved")
DimPlot(combined, group.by = "treatment", cols = c("Vehicle" = "steelblue", "DrugA" = "tomato"))
```

---

## 7. Gene Activity Scores and Annotation

Clusters from peak accessibility alone aren't labeled with cell identities yet.
`Signac::GeneActivity()` estimates per-gene activity by summing accessibility over
each gene's body + upstream promoter region, giving an RNA-like activity score you
can annotate the same way you would real expression:

```r
gene_activities <- GeneActivity(combined)
combined[["ACTIVITY"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = gene_activities)

DefaultAssay(combined) <- "ACTIVITY"
combined <- NormalizeData(combined, normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                          scale.factor = median(combined$nCount_ACTIVITY))
```

With an RNA-like assay in hand, this package's existing annotation functions apply
directly -- they only need an assay with sensible feature names, not RNA specifically.
`MarkerPlot()` (dot plot) and `AnnotateClusters()` (per-cluster UCell scoring) both
work unchanged on the `"ACTIVITY"` assay:

```r
lineage_markers <- data.frame(
  Gene     = c("Cd3e", "Cd3d", "Cd19", "Ms4a1", "Cd14", "Itgam", "Epcam", "Krt8"),
  CellType = c("T cell", "T cell", "B cell", "B cell",
              "Myeloid", "Myeloid", "Epithelial", "Epithelial")
)

MarkerPlot(combined, genes = lineage_markers, assay = "ACTIVITY", cluster = TRUE)

res <- AnnotateClusters(
  combined,
  markers            = list(Tcell = c("Cd3e", "Cd3d"), Bcell = c("Cd19", "Ms4a1"),
                            Myeloid = c("Cd14", "Itgam"), Epithelial = c("Epcam", "Krt8")),
  cluster_col        = "seurat_clusters",
  filter_nonspecific = FALSE,
  min_detection_frac = 0.05,
  return_scores      = "cluster",
  new_col            = "cell_type"
)
combined <- res$obj
table(combined$cell_type)

# Feature-density view of gene activity, same as for real expression elsewhere in this package
DefaultAssay(combined) <- "ACTIVITY"
PlotFeatureDensity(combined, features = c("Cd3e", "Epcam"), reduction = "umap")

DefaultAssay(combined) <- "ATAC"   # switch back for peak-level work below
```

---

## 8. Motif Enrichment — `chromVAR`

Gene activity tells you *what genes look accessible*; motif enrichment (via
`chromVAR`) tells you *which transcription factors' binding sites look accessible*,
per cell -- useful for spotting a regulatory program driving a cluster or condition
rather than a single gene. This is plain Signac/chromVAR, not wrapped by
`SingleCellTools`:

```r
pfm <- TFBSTools::getMatrixSet(
  x    = JASPAR2020::JASPAR2020,
  opts = list(collection = "CORE", tax_group = "vertebrates")
)

combined <- AddMotifs(combined, genome = BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10::BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10,
                     pfm = pfm)
combined <- RunChromVAR(combined, genome = BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10::BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10)

DefaultAssay(combined) <- "chromvar"
# Example: CTCF motif accessibility per cluster (swap in the JASPAR ID you care about)
FeaturePlot(combined, features = "MA0139.1")
VlnPlot(combined, features = "MA0139.1", group.by = "cell_type")

DefaultAssay(combined) <- "ATAC"   # switch back for the rest of this vignette
```

`AddMotifs()`'s querying vertebrate-wide motifs (rather than restricting to one
species) is standard practice here -- DNA-binding motifs are far more conserved
across species than the genes encoding the TFs themselves, so this isn't
mouse-specific despite our data being mouse.

---

## 9. Differential Accessibility Between Conditions

### Per-cell (fast, but pools cells like any per-cell test)

Signac's recommended test for accessibility is logistic regression (`test.use =
"LR"`), controlling for sequencing depth as a latent variable -- the standard
approach for binary-ish, sparse peak data:

```r
Idents(combined) <- combined$treatment

da_peaks <- FindMarkers(
  combined,
  ident.1     = "DrugA",
  ident.2     = "Vehicle",
  test.use    = "LR",
  latent.vars = "nCount_ATAC",
  min.pct     = 0.05
)

# Nearest gene for the top differential peaks
ClosestFeature(combined, regions = rownames(da_peaks)[1:10])
```

The same motif-level test works directly on the `chromvar` assay for differential
motif *activity* rather than differential peak accessibility:

```r
DefaultAssay(combined) <- "chromvar"
da_motifs <- FindMarkers(combined, ident.1 = "DrugA", ident.2 = "Vehicle",
                         test.use = "LR", latent.vars = "nCount_ATAC")
DefaultAssay(combined) <- "ATAC"
```

Like any per-cell test, `FindMarkers()` here treats every cell as an independent
replicate rather than every sample -- the same pseudoreplication concern flagged for
`CompositionAnalysis(test = ...)` elsewhere in this package's vignettes applies to
peak/motif accessibility too.

### Pseudobulk (the sample-respecting alternative)

`PseudobulkDE()` is assay-agnostic -- it aggregates whatever assay you point it at
via `Seurat::AggregateExpression()` and runs `DESeq2` on the per-sample totals, which
works on a peak-count matrix exactly as well as it does on a gene-count matrix. With
2 samples per condition here, this is the test that actually reflects the number of
biological replicates:

```r
pb_atac <- PseudobulkDE(
  combined,
  sample_col    = "orig.ident",
  condition_col = "treatment",
  ident_1       = "DrugA",
  ident_2       = "Vehicle",
  assay         = "ATAC"
)
pb_atac$results                       # DESeq2 results, one row per peak
subset(pb_atac$results, padj < 0.05)
```

---

## 10. Composition Analysis Between Conditions

Whether the cluster/cell-type mix itself shifted between conditions uses the exact
same functions as the RNA/spatial vignettes -- `CompositionAnalysis()`/
`CompositionEstimationPlot()` only need a `group_col`/`sample_col`/`condition_col` on
any Seurat object, ATAC included:

```r
comp <- CompositionAnalysis(
  combined,
  group_col     = "cell_type",
  sample_col    = "orig.ident",
  condition_col = "treatment",
  test          = "chisq"
)
comp$proportions
```

As with every `test = ...` call in this package's other vignettes: this pools cells
across samples per condition, so it emits a `warning()` and shouldn't be read as a
valid replicate-level p-value with only 2 samples per condition here.
`CompositionEstimationPlot()` is the sample-respecting complement -- one point per
`orig.ident` (not per cell), plus a bootstrap 95% CI on the effect size, rather than
a p-value:

```r
CompositionEstimationPlot(comp, idx = c("Vehicle", "DrugA"))
```

See the main vignette's 3.11 section for a full walkthrough of how to read a
`dabestr` estimation plot (the two-panel layout, and what each `effect` option
measures) -- the same plot type is used throughout this package.

---

## 11. Peak-to-Gene Links (Optional)

`Signac::LinkPeaks()` correlates peak accessibility with nearby gene expression
across cells to nominate candidate regulatory links -- it needs a matched RNA assay
on the same cells (e.g. a multiome dataset), which this generic ATAC-only walkthrough
doesn't assume you have. If you do:

```r
combined <- RegionStats(combined, genome = BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10::BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10)
combined <- LinkPeaks(combined, peak.assay = "ATAC", expression.assay = "RNA")
CoveragePlot(combined, region = "Epcam", extend.upstream = 5000, extend.downstream = 5000)
```

---

## 12. Tips Specific to ATAC Data

**`CreateATACObjects()`/`CreateATACObjectsFilter()` support `genome = "mm10"` (default)
or `"hg38"`.** Each requires only the matching `EnsDb`/`BSgenome` package pair to be
installed (optional Suggests dependencies) -- see the note at the top of this vignette.
For any other organism/build, build the `ChromatinAssay` yourself following Signac's
own vignette instead of these two functions.

**Pass `object_names` if `basename(data_dirs)` isn't a good sample label.** Both
functions default to naming the returned list from `basename(data_dirs)`; override it
with `object_names = c(...)` (same length as `data_dirs`) when your folder names aren't
what you want as `orig.ident`/list names downstream.

**The fragments file needs its `.tbi` index alongside it.** `CreateFragmentObject()`
(called internally) expects `fragments.tsv.gz.tbi` in the same directory as
`fragments.tsv.gz`, even though the index path isn't passed explicitly -- this is
standard `cellranger-atac` output, so it's normally already there.

**Check `DepthCor()` before trusting LSI component 1.** It's routinely dominated by
sequencing depth rather than biological signal; dropping it (`dims = 2:30` instead of
`1:30`) is the Signac-recommended default, not a special case.

**`FindTopFeatures(min.cutoff = "q0")` keeps every peak; raise it for a stricter,
faster-to-compute feature set** (e.g. `"q75"` keeps only the top 25% most commonly
used peaks) -- useful on very large peak sets where `RunSVD()` becomes slow.

**`algorithm = 3` (SLM) in `FindClusters()`** is Signac's recommended clustering
algorithm for LSI-based reductions, rather than Seurat's RNA default (Louvain,
`algorithm = 1`).

**Reuse this package's assay-agnostic functions rather than reimplementing them for
ATAC.** `MarkerPlot()`, `AnnotateClusters()`, `PlotFeatureDensity()`,
`CompositionAnalysis()`/`CompositionEstimationPlot()`, and `PseudobulkDE()` all work
unchanged on a `GeneActivity()`-derived assay or the peak assay directly -- there's no
ATAC-specific annotation/composition/DE function in this package because none of the
existing ones needed to be ATAC-specific in the first place.

**`GenerateQCReport()`/`ApplyQCFilters()` work on ATAC metadata columns too.** They
don't hardcode RNA metric names -- point `metadata_cols` at whatever QC columns your
object actually has.

---

## 13. Session Info

```r
sessionInfo()
```

Key packages used in this vignette:

| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| `SingleCellTools` | Object creation (`CreateATACObjects`/`Filter`), QC reporting, and reused assay-agnostic annotation/composition/DE functions |
| `Signac` | Chromatin assay construction, TF-IDF/LSI, gene activity, motif setup |
| `Seurat` | Core data structure, clustering, UMAP, differential expression |
| `harmony` | Batch correction across samples on the LSI embedding |
| `EnsDb.Mmusculus.v79` | Mouse gene annotation (hardcoded inside `CreateATACObjects()`) |
| `BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10` | Mouse genome sequence (hardcoded inside `CreateATACObjects()`; also used for motif matching) |
| `JASPAR2020` / `TFBSTools` | Transcription factor binding motif database |
| `chromVAR` / `motifmatchr` | Per-cell motif accessibility scoring |
| `DESeq2` (via `PseudobulkDE()`) | Pseudobulk differential accessibility |
